# Indonesia remains a wild card  Indonesia is planning to ban mineral exports from 2014 as it would like to see more of the ore processed at home. - A 20% export tax on nickel ore was introduced in May 2012 – but - unclear how much is being borne by buyers. - The tax is based on benchmark prices for different nickel ore grades. - Many companies have put forward plans to build smelters in Indonesia - - infrastructure? - Can Indonesia maintain high grade ore exports further out? # China’s low capital cost difficult to replicate elsewhere

# Summary - Around 30% of global nickel supply is dependent on imported nickel - ore. - •Significant dependence on Indonesia for nickel imports creates risks in line with potential export ban impact. - •We see the Indonesian government introducing further measures to incentivise downstream investment which will increase the cost of nickel ore. - •China’s NPI sector is the largest consumer of seaborne nickel ore. The cost of NPI will rise in line with higher ore and energy prices. - •However, a complete ban by Indonesia would dramatically change the picture for the nickel market. 19
